READABILITY.evidence: Names explain themselves (windowDefinitionsToSQL, assertWindowName, compareBoundaries). Each .window() method has a JSDoc with an example. Formatted with dprint to match the codebase. The only single-letter name is `q` in the test file.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: All spec and validation logic lives in sql/functions/window.ts. Each dialect only adds an optional windows field, a thin .window() method and one windowDefinitionsToSQL(windows) call. The duplicate-name check is repeated in five methods, which is minor and matches the reference.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Validates thoroughly: ntile/nthValue need positive integers, preceding/following reject negative or non-integer values, frames check boundary order and invalid ends, window names cannot be empty, whitespace-only or duplicated. Numeric arguments are written into the SQL, never bound.

C6-02-CASE1.evidence: Purely additive. `windows?: { name: string; spec: WindowSpec }[]` is optional on all five *SelectConfig types, and the same .window(name, spec = {}) exists on pg/mysql/sqlite/singlestore/gel. windowSql is empty when no windows are defined, so other queries' SQL is unchanged. All 566 existing tests pass.
